answer: One wharf load per identity, with a 70-credit bond and a meadow-board manifest of key-bound seals. The jetty gate scans seals from the meadow lot. An auditor checks the scan against the manifest; any gap or duplicate burns the bond, and a twice-claimed seal burns both. First filing costs 26 credits; the kth costs 26+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5021, and 1000 fakes cost 2,523,500 credits plus 70,000 in bonds. A rented-crate ring fails: rented seals sit on the lender manifest, and the jetty scan exposes the claim. An honest loader files once, pays 26, and recovers its bond.
